intro: Wet room installation in Borthwickroad typically costs between £6,000 and £12,000, depending on the size of the bathroom, the complexity of the waterproofing required, and the finish you choose. That might sound like a significant investment for a smaller community, but a well-installed wet room genuinely adds value to a property — both in daily usability and resale appeal. For homeowners in Borthwickroad looking to modernise an ageing bathroom, improve accessibility, or simply make better use of a compact space, a wet room is one of the most practical upgrades available. Getting it right, however, depends heavily on the type of property you're working with — and Borthwickroad has some real variety on that front.
localContext: Borthwickroad sits in Midlothian and has a mix of older stone-built properties, traditional period cottages, and some more modern estate homes, each presenting its own set of challenges when it comes to wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages in Borthwickroad often have solid floors, limited existing drainage infrastructure, and walls that require careful assessment before any tanking or waterproofing work begins. Suspended timber floors — common in older homes — need to be either reinforced or replaced with a suitable substrate before a wet room drain can be properly set into the floor. Modern estate properties in Borthwickroad tend to be more straightforward in terms of floor construction, though they can have tighter joist spacing that affects drainage positioning. Borthwickroad also sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring in when choosing your shower fittings and screen materials, as limescale build-up on exposed surfaces is a genuine long-term consideration — opting for quality fittings with easy-clean coatings will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Borthwickroad starts well before anyone picks up a tool. The first stage is a thorough survey of the existing bathroom space — assessing floor structure, wall condition, existing plumbing routes, and where the waste will drain to. This is where older Borthwickroad properties often need the most attention; some period cottages have drainage that runs in unexpected directions, and getting the fall of the floor right is non-negotiable for a wet room to function properly. Once the survey is complete, the existing bathroom is fully stripped out. If you have a suspended timber floor, this is when it gets reinforced or replaced with a cement board or similar rigid substrate capable of supporting the tanking system. The walls and floor are then tanked — this means applying a waterproof membrane across every surface that water will contact, with particular care taken at junctions between walls and floor where leaks most commonly originate. After tanking, the floor is graded to the drain point, typically a linear drain along one wall or a central point drain, and the screed is laid. Tiling, shower fixtures, and glass screens or panels are then fitted. For Borthwickroad homeowners in older stone properties, ventilation is a key consideration at this stage — solid stone walls don't breathe the same way modern materials do, and a quality extractor fan rated appropriately for the room size helps prevent moisture issues long term. The whole process from strip-out to completion typically takes between five and ten working days.
pricing: In Borthwickroad, most wet room installations fall between £6,000 and £12,000 for a standard bathroom conversion. A straightforward installation in a modern estate home with a concrete floor sits towards the lower end of that range. Converting a period cottage or older stone-built property in Borthwickroad, where floor reinforcement, re-routing of old pipework, and more extensive waterproofing preparation is involved, can push costs toward the higher end or beyond it. The choice of materials matters too — basic but durable tiles and a standard drain are very different in cost to large-format porcelain with a designer linear drain and bespoke glass screen. Always get a detailed written quote that breaks down labour and materials separately.
whyLocal: For a project like wet room installation, local knowledge genuinely counts. A tradesperson familiar with Borthwickroad will have worked in similar stone-built properties and cottages before — they'll know what surprises tend to lurk behind old bathroom walls and under period floors, and they'll plan accordingly rather than discovering problems mid-job. Local tradespeople also tend to be more accountable; they work in the same community and their reputation is built locally. For ongoing aftercare or any snagging issues that come up, someone based near Borthwickroad is far more likely to respond quickly than a firm that travelled in from a distance.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickroad?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern home. The floor structure needs careful assessment, older pipework may need updating, and thorough tanking is essential given the thickness and age of stone walls. It's very achievable with the right tradesperson, and older Borthwickroad properties can look stunning with the right finish.

faqs.q: How does the moderately hard water in Borthwickroad affect a wet room?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water means limescale will gradually build up on shower heads, glass screens, and exposed chrome fittings. It's not a major problem, but it's worth choosing fittings with easy-clean coatings and using a good quality shower head with anti-limescale nozzles. Regular descaling keeps everything looking its best and extends the life of your fittings.

faqs.q: How long will a wet room installation take in a typical Borthwickroad property?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Older properties in Borthwickroad that need additional floor preparation or pipe re-routing tend to sit toward the longer end of that range. Your installer should give you a realistic timeline at the survey stage once they've assessed the specific conditions of your bathroom.

faqs.q: Is a wet room a good investment for a Borthwickroad home?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly if you're upgrading an outdated bathroom in an older stone-built property or period cottage. A well-designed wet room adds practical value and is attractive to buyers. Given the variety of property types in Borthwickroad, a quality wet room can meaningfully differentiate your home, especially if the existing bathroom is tired or poorly laid out.
